packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING: PACKET 05

Isolation: I read this packet's PROMPT.md and inspected only its supplied images and my locally made crops. I did not consult any catalogue, edition, earlier transcription, web source, repository, or proposed identification. No work or author identification is attempted.

Layout survey: Both images are upright photographs of a broad, irregularly edged sheet with a strong central vertical fold. There are two widely separated text blocks, one on either side of the fold; these may be facing leaf areas rather than two columns of one page. I designate them L and R without inferring reading order across the fold. Each has roughly 28 lines in dark ink. Some initials have red strokes, and numerous selected phrases have red underlining. There is no distinct running title. Most writing is one size. Sparse marginal notes and reference-like marks are visible; these are not a continuous surrounding commentary. Image-001 is particularly stained and faded; image-002 has appreciably clearer writing on the right. Holes remove letters, and the outer edges are incomplete. The underlined phrases appear to be quoted or singled-out text embedded in prose; that is an interpretation, not proof of a particular text structure.

Method and crop record: All coordinates below are source pixels (left, top, right, bottom). Native crops were made with Pillow crop(), saved as PNG, and viewed with original detail; no scaling, rotation, sharpening, or contrast modification was used. Paired a/b crops overlap by 50 pixels and constitute the SAME physical lines, not additional text.
image-001.jpg: a_right_top_a (4440,650,6040,1690); a_right_top_b (5990,650,7590,1690).
image-002.jpg: b_left_top_a (620,550,2220,1550); b_left_top_b (2170,550,3770,1550); b_left_mid_a (620,2100,2220,3220); b_left_mid_b (2170,2100,3770,3220); b_right_before_a (4250,2000,5850,3000); b_right_before_b (5800,2000,7400,3000); b_right_mid_a (4250,2900,5850,4050); b_right_mid_b (5800,2900,7400,4050); b_right_after_a (4250,3970,5850,4980); b_right_after_b (5800,3970,7400,4980).

Line numbers count physical text lines from the top of the relevant image text block, separately for L and R; because baselines curve, these counts remain approximate. Pixel locations and the crop record disambiguate them. Abbreviation strokes are rendered with a macron where possible; proposed expansions appear in parentheses; uncertain letter sequences have ?. This is selective transcription, with no silent restoration of gaps.

Coverage and limitations: Both complete images were inspected for layout. Native-scale reading sampled image-001 upper right and image-002 upper/middle left plus most of the middle/lower right. Most of image-001 and image-002 right lines 1-10, the lower-left text, and miscellaneous margins remain unread. The R11-28 passage is the most useful connected sample here, but many words remain uncertain and some expansions are only proposals. Native pixels clarify ductus but do not recover erased or stained ink. An adjacent upper-right crop of image-002 would be useful to establish the preceding argument; improved lighting or a different spectral image would help more than enlargement in the badly stained areas. No author, work, date, or provenance is inferred.
